label: Bladebro upstream version pinned at v4.8.2, published 2026-11-20T16:33:56Z; macOS arm64/x64 assets carry SHA-256 digests; read date 2026-11-21.
Bladebro exposes exactly five tools (act, see, state, run, vision) with CLI reusing the same handlers; page model is see model/content/outline/find/extract and large reads page to artifacts.
Bladebro has console/network/xhr log rings via see logs but no HAR export, no heap/perf trace, no raw CDP passthrough and no Lighthouse; cross-origin iframe content is outside its supported surface.
Bladebro signed-in work uses your-browser mode (bladebro rb on, attach or import profile, page injection off, rb status/pause/off) plus named sessions that save cookies and storage.
Bladebro claims real stealth with anti-detection topics and a published STEALTH_BENCH; neither Chrome DevTools nor Aside documents any stealth or anti-detection feature.

Chrome DevTools (bdg) is the only mode with full raw CDP (300+ methods across 53 domains) and HAR export (bdg network har); its MCP path is a 26-tool subset with isolated instances plus a live --autoConnect instance for signed-in work.

Aside reaches console/network capture only through Playwright page.on events (skip-valid) and documents explicit gaps for HAR, Lighthouse, parallel isolation and raw CDP; its REPL offers Performance API timing only.

Aside owns deterministic signed-in browser work by default: signed-in account prerequisite, --account selection, password autofill, permission modes and human-only MFA/CAPTCHA gates; Chrome live instance is its stated fallback.
Contradiction carried forward: hub router advertises Lighthouse as Chrome DevTools intent, but the 30-feature catalog has no dedicated Lighthouse feature; performance is CDP/script based.
Every upstream Bladebro claim is pinned to v4.8.2 and read date 2026-11-21 because the project ships roughly 40 releases in four months.
